transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Well, I'm here because things have been pretty difficult lately. Ever since my father-in-law moved in with us, I’ve just been snapping at my wife over little house things. I'm also putting off jobs and paperwork that I used to stay right on top of. 

I don't know, I just can’t seem to get my head quiet. Even when I go out in the workshop or try to get some fishing in, I just can't shut my brain off. It's starting to really get to me.
Do these problems seem mainly connected to your father-in-law moving in with you?

Yeah, I'd say so. He moved in with us after he had a fall. And, well, within just the first couple of months of him being there, I noticed I was already falling behind on my paperwork. That's also when I started arguing with my wife over all the household changes. So, yeah, it all really ties back to that.
If your father-in-law were no longer living with you, do you think these problems would mostly go away?

I'd like to think so, but I really can't say for sure. The situation hasn't ended, you know? He's still living with us, and all the caregiving and the changes around the house are still just part of our daily life now. So I haven't actually had a stretch where things were back to normal to see if the problems go away with it.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things, not just your father-in-law living with you?

No, not really. It's pretty much just this whole situation with my father-in-law. I mean, sure, I have the usual stuff I think about, but the only thing that's really keeping my brain spinning and messing with my focus is him being at the house and how much everything has changed.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?
No, not really. I mean, I'm definitely stressed out and frustrated with how things are going at the house, but I wouldn't say I feel sad or depressed. Just overwhelmed by it all, I guess.
Is this stress causing problems with how you function day to day?

Yeah, it definitely is. I actually missed an important filing date for my contractor license recently. I've even had to turn down or delay some small repair jobs because... well, I'm just not keeping up with things the way I used to. And at home, it's taking a toll too. All this strain has put some real tension into my marriage, and I'm finding it a lot harder to just follow through on my normal family responsibilities.
Would you say anxiety is the main feeling you’ve been dealing with in this situation?

I don't know if I'd use the word anxiety. It's really more just... stress, you know? And frustration. I'm not sitting around feeling scared or panicked or anything like that. It's just this constant pressure from the whole situation at the house, and feeling like I can't get a break from it.
